purpose: Verify algebraic robustness of every currently mapped behavioural implementation under structural extreme cases and define sensitivity-analysis prerequisites without inventing empirical parameter ranges or treating form-level tests as model validation.
principles: Form-level stress tests verify implementation properties implied by the equation; they do not validate the equation against the Romanian economy.
Extreme-condition validity for the integrated model remains untested while behavioural closure is inactive.
Sensitivity analysis requires scientifically admissible parameter distributions or ranges and frozen measurement transforms; convenience ranges are prohibited.
A structural bound already implied by an equation, such as a convex weight in [0,1], may be tested without claiming an empirical parameter range.
Passing this contract never authorizes calibration, behavioural closure, feedback activation or policy simulation.
Directional stress tests assume the frozen parameter-sign convention: sensitivity coefficients are non-negative magnitudes and equation operators own the causal signs.

structural_extreme_conditions: refinancing_share=0 returns the previous effective rate exactly
refinancing_share=1 returns the marginal market yield exactly
for refinancing_share in [0,1], the result remains a convex combination of the two input rates
refinancing_share outside [0,1] is rejected
non-finite numerical inputs are rejected
structural_sensitivity_checks: the exact local sensitivity to refinancing_share equals marginal_market_yield - previous_effective_rate
when the marginal yield equals the previous effective rate, changing refinancing_share has no effect

structurally_admissible_axes: sign and magnitude of the marginal-minus-effective rate gap
sensitivity_plan.blocker: m[t] remains unidentified on a matched public repricing ledger, so no empirical uncertainty distribution or calibrated sensitivity run is authorized.

structural_extreme_conditions: with all sensitivities zero, output equals the intercept
with positive income sensitivity, increasing disposable-income growth increases predicted consumption growth
with positive rate sensitivity, increasing the real borrowing rate reduces predicted consumption growth
with positive debt-service sensitivity, increasing the debt-service ratio reduces predicted consumption growth
non-finite inputs or parameters are rejected
structural_sensitivity_checks: local sensitivity to disposable-income growth equals income_sensitivity
local sensitivity to the real borrowing rate equals -rate_sensitivity
local sensitivity to debt-service ratio equals -debt_service_sensitivity

sensitivity_plan.blocker: The aggregate debt-service measure, measurement scale and population bridge are not frozen, so parameter ranges or distributions may not be invented.

structural_extreme_conditions: with all sensitivities zero, output equals the intercept
with positive activity sensitivity, increasing activity growth increases predicted credit growth
with positive rate sensitivity, increasing the real lending rate reduces predicted credit growth
with positive NPL sensitivity, increasing the NPL ratio reduces predicted credit growth
with positive capital sensitivity, increasing the capital buffer increases predicted credit growth
non-finite inputs or parameters are rejected
structural_sensitivity_checks: local sensitivity to activity growth equals activity_sensitivity
local sensitivity to real lending rate equals -rate_sensitivity
local sensitivity to NPL ratio equals -npl_sensitivity
local sensitivity to capital buffer equals capital_sensitivity

sensitivity_plan.blocker: The aggregate demand/supply identification problem, remaining BLS gap, prudential population mismatch and measurement scales remain unresolved.

structural_extreme_conditions: persistence=0 removes the lagged NPL contribution
persistence=1 includes the full lagged NPL contribution
persistence outside [0,1] is rejected
with positive output sensitivity, increasing output growth reduces the predicted NPL change
with positive debt-service sensitivity, increasing debt-service burden increases the predicted NPL change
non-finite inputs or parameters are rejected
structural_sensitivity_checks: local sensitivity to output growth equals -output_sensitivity
local sensitivity to debt-service burden equals debt_service_sensitivity
local sensitivity to the previous NPL ratio equals persistence

sensitivity_plan.blocker: The matched debt-service burden, target population and NPL change/level measurement convention are not frozen for estimation.
